request.spec:
A transfer to a sheet that already has a person with the same name or alias (as names are
compared) now merges the arriving person into them instead of being refused, exactly as a merge
does (claims after theirs, aliases joined, bound figures lost); the other sheet writes
PERSON_TRANSFERRED name=<name> from=<sheet id> then PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>.
request.prompt:

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A transfer to a sheet that already has a person with the same name or alias (as names are
compared) now merges the arriving person into them instead of being refused, exactly as a merge
does (claims after theirs, aliases joined, bound figures lost); the other sheet writes
PERSON_TRANSFERRED name=<name> from=<sheet id> then PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
When a person is transferred to a sheet where someone already has the same name or alias, they're now merged into that person instead of the transfer being refused. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass: the main "transfer merges" test and the three scenario tests.

**What changed**
- **`TransferPerson.java`:** before transferring, it checks whether the person's name or any of their aliases matches a name or alias on the other sheet.
  - If one person there matches, they're merged into that person.
  - If no one matches, the transfer works as before, including the old refusals for a name used elsewhere in the sheet tree or a contact already on the other sheet.
- **`PersonRepository.java`:** a new `transferInto` does the merge. Claims move as they do in a transfer: listed after the other person's claims, renumbered on that sheet, and unbound from statement figures. The arriving person's name and aliases become the other person's aliases. Everything else of theirs is dropped, including grades, terms and contact. I moved the shared claim-moving and clean-up steps out of `transfer` into helpers so both paths use the same code.
- **Audit:** the other sheet now writes `PERSON_MERGED sheet=… by=… from=<name> into=<name>` right after `PERSON_TRANSFERRED`, followed by its rollup lines. `PersonTransferred` carries the name of the person merged into (null when there was no merge).
- **New migration `V62__person_alias_merged_transfer.sql`:** this makes the alias index non-unique. The test expects Ada to end up with both "Addie" and "addie" as aliases, which the old unique-per-sheet index wouldn't allow. Adding an alias by hand is still refused when the sheet already has it, because `addAlias` checks first. That check used to be backed up by the index, so two people adding the same alias at the same moment could now both succeed.

**Cases I decided myself (the request and tests don't cover them)**
- If the arriving person's names match **more than one** person on the other sheet, the transfer is refused.
- If the matching person is **retired**, the transfer is refused, as a normal merge would be.
- If the matching person was changed by someone else in the meantime, the transfer is refused.
- When a merge happens, the contact check is skipped, because the arriving contact is dropped anyway.

No front-end change was needed.
